description: iBwave Design is software for designing indoor and venue wireless networks, such as distributed antenna systems (DAS), small cells, Wi-Fi and public safety networks, in buildings, stadiums and campuses. Designers import floor plans from CAD, PDF or image files, assign materials to walls and surfaces to build a 3D model, and drag network parts from a components database of more than 40,000 modelled elements, such as antennas, small cells, cables, access points and fibre hardware. The software automates link budgets, access point placement, cable routing and length calculations, predicts signal strength, throughput and capacity with its propagation and capacity engines, checks designs for errors and produces compliance reports and 3D maps. iBwave integrated the propagation engine of AWE Communications (now Altair WinProp) in 2007. It links with iBwave Mobile for site surveys, iBwave Unity for project management and a free iBwave Viewer, and comes in Lite, standard and Enterprise editions. iBwave says over 3,000 companies have used it to deliver more than 500,000 indoor wireless networks. Coverage: any building worldwide. Format and access: commercial desktop software with annual maintenance and certification courses. Caveats: proprietary; predictions depend on the accuracy of building models and material properties. Simulation uses: capacity planning and coverage of in-building networks, including public safety radio coverage needed for emergency response inside large buildings. Related records: Altair WinProp provides the propagation engine, and Forsk Atoll and Infovista Planet cover outdoor planning.
